name: Post-purchase Rationalization
description: After choosing or buying, people tend to defend the decision by upgrading the chosen option and downgrading the rejected alternatives. The mind edits evaluations to make the commitment feel better justified.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to onboarding after purchase, review prompts, returns/cancellation flows, subscription justification, and interpreting customer feedback that may become more favorable simply because a choice has already been made.
prevalence_note: Common in consumer-psychology and retention/brand discussions, but less often named directly in general UX practice than adjacent ideas like sunk cost or choice overload.

findings.description: After choosing between similarly attractive alternatives, participants increased the desirability ratings of the chosen option and decreased the ratings of the rejected option, with larger shifts after more difficult choices — a classic postdecision rationalization effect.
findings.source_title: Postdecision changes in the desirability of alternatives.
findings.source_venue: The Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology
